records.description_rewritten: Rahmer See at Duisburg-Rahm is a real recreation lake and woodland. A 27 July 2026 first-person poster said they had repeatedly visited recently but found almost nobody; a 22 February poster says they often visit but describes no encounter. A 2018 comment claiming to represent local associations describes shores as private land and warns against unauthorised access; this claim is not independently verified property documentation. Duisburg city documents a 2026 lake bathing ban outside its three authorised lidos, which excludes Rahmer See.
records.place_type: gravel lake and adjoining wooded area

independent_and_supplementary_evidence.note: City lists Rahmer See (Großenbaum) among lakes, not authorised lidos.
All Duisburg open lakes outside designated lidos prohibit swimming; danger of steep slopes and cold water.

records.access_information: Swimming at Rahmer See prohibited by Duisburg's 2026 lake policy. Land ownership and private shore access must be checked; avoid club land, no public-sex permission.

records.description_rewritten: Angermunder Baggerloch near Rodendeich/Heiderweg has a long history of gay naturist and cruising discussion. A first-person visitor on 13 July 2026 described men in the area and a signed or marked gay shoreline, and considered adjacent woodland cruising disappointing; that is recent presence evidence, not an independently observed encounter. The city of Düsseldorf explicitly bans swimming in both Angermund gravel-pit lakes because of dangerous depth/cold-water changes; a 2026 local news report describes a fatality in late June. Municipality has also stressed site rules, habitat protection and lack of proper vehicle parking.
records.place_type: gravel pit lakes and informal gay naturist shore

2021 visitor signage and environmental protections, no proper car parking.
